newsitem.title: UK: Brit Biotech shares continue slide.
newsitem.headline: Brit Biotech shares continue slide.

text.p: Shares in drugs group British Biotech Plc continued to slide on Thursday morning amid concerns over the timing of the launch of the company's two main products.

The stock was down 17 pence, or 9.2 percent, at 168 1/2 in midmorning trading after losing 7.7 percent on Wednesday when it announced full-year results. It touched a fresh 12-month low of 157 earlier, and has slid 55 percent from its May 1996 peak of 377 pence.

Traders said heavy selling in the U.S. and UK had driven the stock down after the company indicated that the launch of its lead drug, pancreatitis treatment Zacutex, could be delayed by 12 months in the U.S, with cancer drug Marimastat at least six months behind some analysts' forecasts.
Analaysts said the altered timings had been seized on by bears in the market as a excuse to sell the stock, which is heavily dependent on the two drugs for its valuation.
However one analyst said: "We are still confident that the drugs do work and the issue is one of slippage."

The fall in British Biotech's valuation comes against a background a generally weak biotech sector, which is still reeeling from the failure of a joint Celltech Group Plc and Bayer AG product for septic shock in May.
